minor.issue: The running backend's APP_URL is https://b36e96df-...preview.emergentagent.com. It comes from /etc/supervisor/conf.d/supervisord.conf environment=APP_URL and takes precedence over backend/.env APP_URL (cricket-stats-188...), because load_dotenv does not override. As a result, the PDF red-note link and the report/maintenance email links point to the old preview domain. This is environment configuration. Check APP_URL in deployment, or call load_dotenv(override=True) if .env should win.

asyncio.create_task(notify_users(...)) does not keep a reference to the task, so it can be garbage-collected. Sending is sequential and in-process (SMTP takes ~1.5s per user plus a 0.5s sleep). With many users, a backend restart or hot reload during the send loses the rest of the batch, and those email_logs stay 'queued' with no resume. Consider a persisted queue/job.

issues: bowling-side-on.mp4 is 9.6 MB for 5s (~15 Mbps), while the batting demo is 0.4 MB. Re-encode it (e.g. CRF 28, 720p) for mobile users.
Copy reads 'Up to 1 video(s)'. This is awkward and could be pluralised properly.

critical_code_review_comments: core.get_object: if _fetch_object raises, the per-path lock is never popped from _obj_locks (small leak). On a cold cache, the first Range request waits for the whole object to download.
core.get_object: the cache can hold up to 300 MB per worker process. Each insert recomputes the total size with sum() over all entries (fine at the current scale).

deliver_report now always attaches the PDF regardless of the pdf_export entitlement (as requested). This means free-tier users get the PDF by email even if PDF download is a paid feature. Confirm this is the intended business rule.
Legal 'Last updated' date is hard-coded in constants/legal.js. That is fine, but it must be bumped manually when the content changes.
